LMGTE.title: Rugolo passes Bertolini late as AF Corse wins LMGTE at Silverstone
LMGTE.dek: Cameron, Griffin and Rugolo won LMGTE for AF Corse after Rugolo passed pole-sitter Bertolini’s SMP Ferrari late in the race, with IMSA Performance Matmut’s Porsche taking third.

facts.v: Bertolini’s 1:57.970 put the SMP Ferrari #72 on pole, six tenths clear of Zampieri’s JMW Ferrari #66 in second.

facts.v: Griffin cut a gap of just under ten seconds to Shaitar’s #72 and took the lead round the outside with a little over an hour left.

facts.t: Safety car with 45 minutes to go
facts.v: The crash of the leading LMP2 car brought out the safety car with roughly 45 minutes left, and the restart came with 22 minutes remaining.

chapters.title: Thirteen cars, eight of them Ferraris
text: Thirteen cars made up the LMGTE field for the four-hour season opener, and eight of them were Ferrari 458 Italias. After the Paul Ricard test and the Balance of Performance decisions the Ferrari looked the car to beat.

Matt Griffin, the reigning ELMS GTE champion, had moved to AF Corse to share the #55 with Duncan Cameron and Michele Rugolo. SMP Racing’s #72 paired Andrea Bertolini with Viktor Shaitar and Sergey Zlobin, a trio that looked formidable on paper, although Bertolini, as the Platinum driver, was limited to roughly one stint. Gulf Racing arrived with a Porsche, the #86, and an Aston Martin, the #85, after moving over from the Blancpain Endurance Series, while Fabien Barthez was in the Sofrev-ASP Ferrari #58.

chapters.title: Bertolini on pole by six tenths
text: LMGTE shared its 20-minute session with GTC, and all 27 GT cars set a time. Bertolini put the SMP Ferrari #72 on pole with a 1:57.970 around the halfway point, a lap nobody else came close to. Zampieri took JMW’s #66 second on 1:58.590, 0.620 seconds behind, with Griffin third in the #55 on 1:58.835 and Ayari fourth for Sofrev-ASP on 1:59.166. Cressoni was fifth for Kessel on 1:59.471.
Nine cars were inside two seconds of pole, the last of them Kaffer’s AT Racing Ferrari #56 on 1:59.803, while the Gulf Aston Martin #85 qualified last of the class on 2:04.701.

chapters.title: Lyons takes charge from the pole car
text: McKenzie’s JMW Ferrari was in front within two minutes, with Zlobin’s #72 behind him, but the pole car then slid back, caught by Lyons’s AF Corse Ferrari #54 and later by Narac’s IMSA Performance Matmut Porsche #76. Lyons made a bold move into Vale past Kessel’s #81, then passed McKenzie at Club to lead the class after about nine minutes. After one hour the top five were the #54, #76, #82, #81 and #66.

chapters.title: A ten-second class
text: Ten seconds covered the top six at one point in the second hour. Perrodo took the Crubile Sport Porsche #82 past Perazzini’s #54 for the lead just before the AF Corse Ferrari made its stop. Rugolo then took the lead back for AF Corse in the #55, diving up the inside of McKenzie’s JMW Ferrari at Vale.

chapters.title: Griffin reels in Shaitar
text: By the middle of the third hour Shaitar was leading in the #72 and Griffin, in the #55, was closing: just under ten seconds behind, then five. With a little over an hour to go Griffin went round the outside of the loop and Shaitar ran wide on the exit, handing AF Corse the lead. A later stop cost a few seconds, as Griffin had to overshoot his box with Lyons pitting alongside.
Lyons got the #54 past Barthez’s Sofrev Ferrari #58 for fifth, and Hall was briefly the fastest GT driver on track in the Gulf Aston Martin #85 despite running tenth in class.

chapters.title: Safety car reshuffles the pack
text: With an hour to go the class ran #72, #55, #56, #58 and #76, and the race changed shape with roughly 45 minutes left, when the leading LMP2 car crashed heavily on the approach to the Hangar Straight as it lapped Rugolo’s #55. The safety car brought the field together, and only four LMGTE cars were left on the lead lap when the race went green again with 22 minutes remaining.

chapters.title: Rugolo passes Bertolini
text: Bertolini was at the wheel of the pole car for the closing stint and led the restart with Rugolo right behind. The decisive moment came with about 16 minutes to go: Bertolini lost time in a tangle with Cioci’s AF Corse Ferrari #54 at Aintree, and Rugolo took the #55 into the lead. SMP could not turn pole into victory, and the #72 finished second on the same lap. IMSA Performance Matmut’s #76, with Narac, Armindo and Hallyday, took third a lap behind the winner.

chapters.title: AF Corse’s win, SMP’s near miss
text: The #55 of Cameron, Griffin and Rugolo won on 112 laps, with Bertolini, Shaitar and Zlobin second on the same lap and the #76 third on 111. Behind them came AT Racing’s #56 and JMW’s #66, also on 111, then the AF Corse #54 and the Sofrev-ASP #58 on 110, with all 13 cars classified. Rugolo set the class fastest lap, 2:00.077.

Rugolo said the contact between Bertolini and another Ferrari had helped him, while Griffin reckoned he had passed the SMP car three times in total. Before the race Bertolini had suggested the Porsches would be quicker at Imola, where the series went next on 18 May.

GTC.title: Pier Guidi hauls Team Ukraine to the GTC win at Silverstone
GTC.dek: Kruglyk, Chukanov and Pier Guidi won GTC for Team Ukraine after Pier Guidi retook the lead from Formula Racing following the safety car, with SMP Racing’s #73 Ferrari second.

facts.v: Persiani’s 2:00.032 earned pole for the SMP Ferrari #71, but the car was held in the pit lane at the start and retired.
Pier Guidi said the safety car cost Team Ukraine its advantage and a wheel change dropped the car from first to second before he caught the leader.

chapters.title: Fifteen entries and five makes
text: GTC arrived as a very healthy 15-car class with five manufacturers represented: Ferrari, McLaren, Porsche, BMW and Audi. One of SMP Racing’s three Ferraris was withdrawn before the race, leaving 14 cars in the results, eight of them Ferrari 458 Italia GT3s. SMP was defending its 2013 title and entered the #73 for Beretta, Markozov and Anton Ladygin, who had moved across from the #71, where Persiani took his place beside Kirill Ladygin and Basov.

Team Ukraine, new to the series, ran a Ferrari for Kruglyk, Chukanov and Pier Guidi. ART Grand Prix fielded two McLarens, the #98 for Korjus, Demoustier and Goudy and the #99 for Ricardo Gonzalez, Ajlani and Brundle, while Team Russia by Barwell ran a BMW Z4 for Machitski, Sardarov and Cocker. Formula Racing brought an all-Danish Ferrari crew of Magnussen, Laursen and Mac, Sebastien Loeb Racing an Audi R8 LMS ultra, and Pro GT by Almeras a Porsche for Perera, Lasserre and Dermont. Prospeed Competition had switched its Porsche from GTE to GTC.

chapters.title: Persiani edges Pier Guidi
text: Pier Guidi was on top of the GTC order in the 20-minute session, which GTC shared with LMGTE, before Persiani answered with a 2:00.032 in the SMP Ferrari #71 with about three minutes left. He had run wide on his second lap and had to cool the tyres before going again. Pier Guidi was second on 2:00.209, less than two tenths away, with AF Corse’s #63 of Lind third on 2:00.676, Cocker’s Barwell BMW #78 fourth and Korjus’s McLaren #98 fifth.

Team Ukraine had been fastest in the second practice session on Friday, ahead of the SMP Ferrari and the Prospeed Porsche, and that pace carried through to Saturday. In the same session AF Corse’s #95 made contact with an LMP2 Morgan at Vale, which was repaired overnight.

chapters.title: The pole car stays in the pits
text: Pole did not translate into a start: the #71 missed the start and Team Ukraine’s #96 took the front slot instead. Demoustier led the class early in the ART McLaren #98, and by the half-hour mark the order was #73, #96 and #75. After the first stops Prospeed’s Porsche led, from the #96, Formula Racing’s #60, the Barwell BMW #78 and the Audi #51.

chapters.title: Trouble for the chasers
text: The #98 McLaren crawled down the Hangar Straight with a puncture, and the Audi #51 slowed on the same stretch after a spin on the exit of the loop. Barwell’s BMW ran wide at Stowe and ripped up turf. By the start of the final hour the shuffle of stops had put Team Ukraine in front, with Formula Racing and the SMP #73 close behind.

chapters.title: Safety car and a wheel change
text: With an hour to go the order was #96, #60, #73, #51, #75. The safety car, called with roughly 45 minutes left after a crash among the LMP2 runners, undid Team Ukraine’s lead. A wheel change dropped the #96 to second, and Formula Racing’s Ferrari passed it in the pit lane. Only three GTC cars were on the lead lap when the race restarted with 22 minutes remaining.

chapters.title: Pier Guidi reels in the Danes
text: Pier Guidi, who had two stints in the car, caught and passed the Formula Racing Ferrari with about 11 minutes left, and the Danes were then picked off by Markozov in the SMP Ferrari #73 for second before the end. Team Ukraine took the flag on 109 laps. Pier Guidi said there was just enough time after the restart to catch the leader.

chapters.title: Ukraine win, SMP climbs from 12th
text: The #96 of Kruglyk, Chukanov and Pier Guidi won on 109 laps. SMP Racing’s #73 of Beretta, Markozov and Ladygin finished second on the same lap after starting 12th in the class, with Magnussen, Laursen and Mac third for Formula Racing, also on 109. Barwell’s BMW #78 was fourth a lap down. The McLaren #99, the Audi #51, the McLaren #98, the Pro GT Porsche #93 and the Prospeed Porsche #75 followed on 107 laps, ahead of the AF Corse #63 and Sofrev-ASP #59 on 106 and the AF Corse pair of #95 and #62 on 102. Lind set the class fastest lap in the #63, 2:02.044.
The #71 was the only retirement. The second of five rounds follows at Imola on 18 May.
